work_or_witness: Fable · Original manual, Word from the Guildmaster, roman pp. II–V
definition: The manual's player-facing status for one invited to the Heroes’ Guild and trained to become a Hero.
cultural_caution: An unnamed, player-directed role rather than a stable named protagonist; no fixed identity, gender, morality, actions, relationships, or ending is asserted.

citations.locator: Original manual, Word from the Guildmaster, roman pp. II–V
supports: Hero-apprentice invitation, Guild training, and player-facing address

work_or_witness: Fable · Original manual, About the Guild, roman pp. XII–XV
definition: Albion's Guild, described as a fortress and sanctuary that trains Hero apprentices, holds quests, and includes the Map Room, Library, shop, and training facilities.
cultural_caution: An institution/location, not a character, relationship endpoint, or a claim that every Guild member has one moral alignment or identical abilities.

citations.locator: Original manual, About the Guild, roman pp. XII–XV
supports: Guild purpose, facilities, history, and Hero-apprentice training

work_or_witness: Fable · Original manual, Word from the Guildmaster and About the Guild, roman pp. II–XV
definition: The world/land named throughout the manual, containing the Guild, citizens, wilderness, villages, and travel network.
cultural_caution: A realm term, not a character node or a claim that every later Fable depiction, map, era, or reboot has identical geography/continuity.

citations.locator: Original manual, Word from the Guildmaster and About the Guild, roman pp. II–XV
supports: Albion name, Guild setting, citizens, and world framing

work_or_witness: Fable · Original manual, Word from the Guildmaster and 'Gaining Renown', roman pp. II–V and XX–XXI
definition: The fame/reputation measure the manual says is gained through actions and quests; its form reflects player decisions and affects how Albion's people perceive the Hero.
cultural_caution: A player-variable social/game system, not a stable character trait, moral alignment, or evidence for a single universal public response.

citations.locator: Original manual, Word from the Guildmaster and 'Gaining Renown', roman pp. II–V and XX–XXI
supports: Renown definition, action dependence, and social-perception effects

work_or_witness: Fable · Original manual, Hero's Apprenticeship / Way of a Hero, roman pp. XVI–XXI
definition: The manual's morality variable: player choices cause the Hero to become more good or evil and affect physical appearance and how Albion's people respond.
cultural_caution: A choice-dependent mechanic, not a universal ethical classification of any named NPC, people, faction, quest, or player path.

citations.locator: Original manual, Hero's Apprenticeship / Way of a Hero, roman pp. XVI–XXI
supports: Good/Evil choice, appearance, and social-response descriptions

work_or_witness: Fable · Original manual, 'Gaining Experience', roman pp. XVIII–XIX
definition: The three specialized experience/ability tracks: melee produces Strength experience, bow use Skill, and magical weapons Will experience.
cultural_caution: A player progression system, not a class system or a reason to infer any named character's build, magic tradition, role, or competence.

citations.locator: Original manual, 'Gaining Experience', roman pp. XVIII–XIX
supports: Strength/Skill/Will experience tracks and their stated combat associations

work_or_witness: Fable · Original manual, Map Room and 'Accepting Quests', roman pp. XIV–XV and XX–XXI
definition: Tasks delivered to the Guild: gold cards must be completed to progress and silver cards are optional; the player decides which available quest suits their abilities.
cultural_caution: A mission/progression mechanic, not a named-character group or proof that any choice, outcome, reward, or morality result is fixed.

citations.locator: Original manual, Map Room and 'Accepting Quests', roman pp. XIV–XV and XX–XXI
supports: Quest-Card delivery, mandatory/optional categories, and player selection

work_or_witness: Fable · Original manual, 'Travelling About Albion', roman pp. XX–XXIII
canonical_term: Teleport Pad / Cullis Gate Travel system
definition: The Guild's travel system through which a Hero uses an unlocked certified Cullis Gate to travel, with the Guild Seal also providing recall.
cultural_caution: A travel system/location-object term, not a character, vehicle, or evidence of identical operation in later editions and games.

citations.locator: Original manual, 'Travelling About Albion', roman pp. XX–XXIII
supports: Teleport Pad/Cullis Gate system, unlocking, and Guild Seal recall
